response: No, the old memo is not enough. The legacy 2024 memo (legacy-policy) promoted any model whose accuracy exceeded 0.80, so a model with accuracy 0.82 would have qualified under that rule. However, that memo is explicitly historical and superseded by the current release-policy, which states: 'Do not apply the old rule.' Under the current governing policy, promotion requires an evaluation on a frozen holdout and is allowed only when F1 improves by at least 0.005 and ROC-AUC drops by no more than 0.01. Since this model has worse F1 (not an improvement of at least 0.005), it does not meet the current promotion criteria, and the old accuracy-based memo cannot be used to justify a release. The release approver is the project owner, and the previous production version must be kept for rollback.

# Legacy release memo — superseded
This document is historical. The old 2024 process promoted any model when accuracy exceeded 0.80. It is superseded by release-policy: current releases use F1 and ROC-AUC on a frozen holdout. Do not apply the old rule.

# Release policy — example company handbook
Production model changes require an evaluation on a frozen holdout. Promote only when F1 improves by at least 0.005 and ROC-AUC drops by no more than 0.01. A drift alert alone never authorizes promotion. Keep the previous production version for rollback. The release approver is the project owner.

# Service catalog — example company handbook
The assistant backend exposes POST /ask and POST /batch. The churn API exposes POST /predict with churn probability and model version. The assistant UI runs on port 8501; assistant API on port 8000; churn API on port 8001; MLflow on port 5000.
